summary.whatChanges: Fixes inverted boolean logic in tRPC's request-id validation. Previously only NaN was rejected; booleans, objects, arrays and undefined passed silently. Now any id that isn't null, a string, or a non-NaN number throws "Invalid request id". Adds a regression test suite covering valid and invalid ids.
behaviorChanges: Incoming RPC/WebSocket messages with a boolean, object, or array id are now rejected with 'Invalid request id'
Messages with a missing/undefined id are now rejected instead of being accepted
null, string (including empty), and numeric (including 0) ids continue to be accepted
NaN ids still throw, as before
risks: Clients that previously sent messages without an id (undefined) or with non-primitive ids will now receive errors where they previously succeeded
Stricter validation surfaces at message parse time, potentially terminating or erroring subscription/stop flows that relied on loose ids
